literal: Twelfth month, day gengzi: an edict ordered Mobile-Circuit Attendant Yu Hui to return his army and attack Xing Shuo, halting at Lixia.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengzi day, an edict ordered Yu Hui, mobile-circuit attendant, to return his army and attack Xing Shuo, halting at Lixia.

literal: That year the remnant band of Ge Rong, Han Lou, again held Youzhou in rebellion.
idiomatic: That year Han Lou, a remnant of Ge Rong's band, again held You in rebellion.

literal: First month of spring of the second year, day jiayin: Yu Hui's commander Peng Le led more than two thousand cavalry north to Han Lou, and the army then withdrew.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the second year, on jiayin day, Peng Le, commander under Yu Hui, led more than two thousand cavalry north to Han Lou, and the army then withdrew.

literal: Second month, day guimao, new moon: an edict said that palace guard officials who had merit in the campaign or wounds were to be advanced first at selection.
idiomatic: On guimao day, the new moon of the second month, an edict said that palace guard officials who had merit in the campaign or wounds were to be advanced first at selection.

literal: day jiawu: the late Emperor, the Emperor's father, was honored as Emperor Wenmu, temple name Suzu; the late Empress, the Emperor's mother, as Empress Wenmu.
idiomatic: On jiawu day the late emperor, the emperor's father, was honored as Emperor Wenmu, temple name Suzu; the late empress, the emperor's mother, as Empress Wenmu.

literal: The people of Yan province, Wang Qingzu, gathered a host at Shangdang and styled himself king.
idiomatic: Wang Qingzu of Yan province gathered a host at Shangdang and styled himself king.

literal: Pillar Grand General Erzhu Rong attacked, captured him.
idiomatic: Pillar Grand General Erzhu Rong attacked and captured him.

literal: day renyin: an edict made Palace Attendant of Regular Attendance Prince of Jiyin Huiye concurrently act as mobile-circuit director of the secretariat, supervising Commanders Li Delong and Qiu Daqian in guarding Liang province.
idiomatic: On renyin day an edict made Huiye, palace attendant of regular attendance and Prince of Jiyin, concurrently act as mobile-circuit director of the secretariat, supervising Li Delong and Qiu Daqian in guarding Liang.

literal: Third month, day renxu: an edict ordered Grand General, Prince of Shangdang Tianmu, and Qi Xianwu Wang to attack Xing Shuo.
idiomatic: On renxu day in the third month an edict ordered Tianmu, grand general and Prince of Shangdang, and Qi Xianwu Wang to attack Xing Shuo.

literal: Fourth month of summer, day guimao: the spirit tablets of Suzu Emperor Wenmu and Empress Wenmu were moved to the Grand Temple; officials within and without all received a general promotion of one rank.
idiomatic: On guimao day in the fourth month of summer the spirit tablets of Suzu Emperor Wenmu and Empress Wenmu were moved to the Grand Temple; officials within and without all received a general promotion of one rank.

literal: A partial amnesty within the capital region: death through exile was reduced one degree; penal servitude and below were all remitted.
idiomatic: A partial amnesty in the capital region cut death and exile sentences by one degree and freed all penal servitude and below.

literal: day gengzi: an edict ordered a general promotion of two ranks for officers and soldiers under Prince of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong.
idiomatic: On gengzi day an edict ordered a general promotion of two ranks for officers and soldiers under Prince of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong.

literal: day xinchou: Prince of Shangdang Tianmu and Qi Xianwu Wang greatly defeated Xing Shuo at Jinan in Qi province; Shuo surrendered, was sent to the capital, and beheaded in the marketplace.
idiomatic: On xinchou day Prince of Shangdang Tianmu and Qi Xianwu Wang greatly defeated Xing Shuo at Jinan in Qi; Shuo surrendered, was sent to the capital, and beheaded in the marketplace.

literal: Yuan Hao took and held Kaocheng, capturing Mobile-Circuit Attendant Yuan Huiye and Commander Qiu Daqian.
idiomatic: Yuan Hao took Kaocheng, capturing Yuan Huiye, mobile-circuit attendant, and Commander Qiu Daqian.

literal: Fifth month, day renzi, new moon: Yuan Hao took Liang province.
idiomatic: On renzi day, the new moon of the fifth month, Yuan Hao took Liang province.

literal: day dingsi: General Who Guards the Army, former Regional Inspector of Xuzhou Yang Yu, was made bearer of the staff of authority, General Who Pacifies the East, and grand commander of the southeastern route, leading troops to guard Xingyang;
idiomatic: On dingsi day Yang Yu, general who guards the army and former regional inspector of Xu, was made bearer of the staff, general who pacifies the east, and grand commander of the southeastern route, leading troops to guard Xingyang;

literal: Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Erzhu Shilong guarded Hulao;
idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong, right vice director of the secretariat, guarded Hulao;

literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Erzhu Shicheng guarded Mount Yao.
idiomatic: Erzhu Shicheng, attendant-in-ordinary, guarded Mount Yao.

literal: day xinyou: an edict on preferential rank and office for those with private horses and arms who followed the campaign.
idiomatic: On xinyou day an edict on preferential rank and office for those with private horses and arms who followed the campaign.

literal: day renxu: another edict recruited soldiers according to the campaign against Ge Rong.
idiomatic: On renxu day another edict recruited soldiers according to the campaign against Ge Rong.

literal: day jiazi: another edict said that officeholders and commoners who furnished horses received preferential ranks in differing degrees.
idiomatic: On jiazi day another edict said that officeholders and commoners who furnished horses received preferential ranks in differing degrees.

literal: day yichou: martial law within and without.
idiomatic: On yichou day martial law was proclaimed within and without.

literal: day guiyou: Yuan Hao took Xingyang and captured Yang Yu.
idiomatic: On guiyou day Yuan Hao took Xingyang and captured Yang Yu.

literal: Erzhu Shilong abandoned Hulao and fled back.
idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong abandoned Hulao and fled back.

literal: day jiaxu: the imperial carriage toured north; day yihai: it reached Henei.
idiomatic: On jiaxu day the imperial carriage toured north; on yihai day it reached Henei.

literal: day bingzi: Yuan Hao entered Luoyang.
idiomatic: On bingzi day Yuan Hao entered Luoyang.

literal: day dingchou: state-founding Duke of Chengyang Zhi was advanced to Prince of Pingyuan; state-founding Marquis of Anchang Chi was made Prince of Huashan; both were given Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
idiomatic: On dingchou day Zhi, state-founding Duke of Chengyang, was advanced to Prince of Pingyuan; Chi, state-founding Marquis of Anchang, was made Prince of Huashan; both were given palace attendant of the third rank.

literal: day wuyin: Mobile-Circuit Attendant Cui Xiaofen and Grand Commander Diao Xuan defeated Yuan Hao's rear-army commander Hou Xuan at Liang province, beheaded him, and captured three thousand of his troops.
idiomatic: On wuyin day Cui Xiaofen, mobile-circuit attendant, and Grand Commander Diao Xuan defeated Yuan Hao's rear-army commander Hou Xuan at Liang, beheaded him, and captured three thousand troops.

literal: Attendant-in-ordinary, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Erzhu Shilong, was made bearer of the staff of authority, mobile-circuit vice director of the secretariat, general of his former post, and regional inspector of Xiang, guarding Ye city with discretionary authority.
idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong, attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and right vice director of the secretariat, was made bearer of the staff, mobile-circuit vice director of the secretariat, general of his former post, and regional inspector of Xiang, guarding Ye with discretionary authority.

literal: Another edict said that in Shangdang those below a hundred and above ninety received third-rank commandery plaque; above eighty, fourth-rank commandery; above seventy, fifth-rank commandery.
idiomatic: Another edict in Shangdang conferred third-rank commandery plaque on those under a hundred and ninety or more; fourth-rank at eighty; fifth-rank at seventy.

literal: Prince of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong met the imperial carriage at Changzi and the same day turned his banners back.
idiomatic: Prince of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong met the emperor at Changzi and turned his banners back the same day.

literal: Prince of Shangdang Tianmu crossed north and met the imperial carriage at Henei.
idiomatic: Prince of Shangdang Tianmu crossed north and met the imperial carriage at Henei.

literal: Sixth month, day jichou: Palace Attendant of the Third Rank Fei Mu was killed by Hao.
idiomatic: On jichou day in the sixth month Fei Mu, palace attendant of the third rank, was killed by Hao.

literal: day renyin: Henei was taken; Administrator Yuan Xi and Commander Zhensun were beheaded.
idiomatic: On renyin day Henei was taken; Administrator Yuan Xi and Commander Zhensun were beheaded.

literal: Seventh month of autumn, day wuchen: Commanders Erzhu Zhao and Heba Sheng crossed from Shixia by night, defeated Hao's son Guanshou and Prince of Anfeng Yanming's army; Yuan Hao was defeated and fled.
idiomatic: On wuchen day in the seventh month of autumn Commanders Erzhu Zhao and Heba Sheng crossed from Shixia by night, defeated Hao's son Guanshou and Prince of Anfeng Yanming's army; Yuan Hao was defeated and fled.

literal: day gengwu: the imperial carriage entered and dwelt at Hualin Park, ascended the Great Summer Gate, and proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On gengwu day the imperial carriage entered Hualin Park, ascended the Great Summer Gate, and proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.

literal: Bearer of the staff of authority, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Commander, state-founding Duke of Yingchuan Erzhu Zhao, was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao, bearer of the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, commander, and state-founding Duke of Yingchuan, was made grand general of chariots and cavalry and palace attendant of the third rank.

literal: An edict said that merit registers of the former court were much falsely claimed; they should all be burned; if achievement was clearly established and known to the age, separate rewards in kind would be given.
idiomatic: An edict said that merit registers of the former court were much falsely claimed and should all be burned; if achievement was clearly established and known to the age, separate rewards in kind would be given.

literal: Foreign guests and frontier chiefs who turned cities and surrendered, with merit not yet recorded, were not within the limit of burning.
idiomatic: Foreign guests and frontier chiefs who turned in cities and surrendered, with merit still unrecorded, were excepted from the burning.

literal: Northern soldiers and civil and military officials who followed the carriage, and those who established righteousness at Mazhu, [7] received a general promotion of five ranks;
idiomatic: Soldiers from the north and civil and military officials who followed the carriage, and those who took up righteousness at Mazhu, [7] all received a general promotion of five ranks;

literal: executive officials of Hebei, two ranks;
idiomatic: executive officials in Hebei, two ranks;

literal: those of Henan who established righteousness and officials who welcomed the carriage, and also those who escorted midway, likewise two ranks.
idiomatic: those in Henan who took up righteousness, officials who welcomed the carriage, and escorts along the route likewise received two ranks.

literal: day renshen: Pillar Grand General, Prince of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong, was made Pillar of Heaven Grand General, with front and rear feathered canopy and martial pipes added.
idiomatic: On renshen day Pillar Grand General Prince of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong was made Pillar of Heaven Grand General, with front and rear feathered canopy and martial pipes added.

literal: day guiyou: Jiang Feng, a soldier of Linying county, beheaded Yuan Hao and sent his head to the capital.
idiomatic: On guiyou day Jiang Feng, a soldier of Linying county, beheaded Yuan Hao and sent his head to the capital.

literal: day jiaxu: Grand General, Prince of Shangdang Tianmu, was made Grand Preceptor; Minister over the Masses, Prince of Chengyang Hui, was made Grand Marshal and Minister of Works.
idiomatic: On jiaxu day Tianmu, grand general and Prince of Shangdang, was made grand preceptor; Hui, minister over the masses and Prince of Chengyang, was made grand marshal and minister of works.

literal: day yihai: at the Capital Pavilion a feast rewarded Pillar of Heaven Grand General Erzhu Rong, Prince of Shangdang Tianmu, and the northern commanders; three hundred palace women and tens of thousands of bolts of silk and brocade of mixed colors were distributed with differing allotments.
idiomatic: On yihai day at the Capital Pavilion a feast rewarded Pillar of Heaven Grand General Erzhu Rong, Prince of Shangdang Tianmu, and the northern commanders; three hundred palace women and tens of thousands of bolts of silk and brocade were distributed with differing allotments.

literal: Also, envoys from provinces and commanderies who presented memorials at the traveling palace all received one major rank.
idiomatic: Envoys from provinces and commanderies who presented memorials at the traveling palace also each gained one major rank.

literal: day dingchou: Yuan Hao's younger brother Xu was captured, [8] and beheaded in the marketplace.
idiomatic: On dingchou day Yuan Hao's younger brother Xu was captured, [8] and beheaded in the marketplace.

literal: An edict stripped all titles, rewards, and ranks given to those who had served Yuan Hao.
idiomatic: An edict rescinded every title, reward, and rank granted to those who had followed Yuan Hao.

literal: day jimao: General Who Pacifies the East, Regional Inspector of Southern Qing Yuan Xu, was made Prince of Xiangcheng; General Who Pacifies the South, Regional Inspector of Southern Yan Yuan Xian, was made Prince of Ruyang.
idiomatic: On jimao day Xu, general who pacifies the east and regional inspector of southern Qing, was made Prince of Xiangcheng; Xian, general who pacifies the south and regional inspector of southern Yan, was made Prince of Ruyang.

literal: Intercalary month, day xinsi: the Emperor first dwelt within the palace.
idiomatic: On xinsi day in the intercalary month the emperor first dwelt within the palace.

literal: day xinmao: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, concurrently Director of the Ministry of Personnel Yang Jin, was made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: On xinmao day Yang Jin, grand general of chariots and cavalry and concurrently director of the ministry of personnel, was made minister of works.

literal: Yan Shixin, regional inspector of Ba, held the south of the province in rebellion; Xiao Yan sent his generals Xiao Wan, Zhang Hong, Jiang Maoda, and others with troops to aid him.
idiomatic: Yan Shixin, regional inspector of Ba, rebelled and held the south of the province; Xiao Yan sent generals Xiao Wan, Zhang Hong, Jiang Maoda, and others to relieve him.

literal: Eighth month, day gengxu, new moon: an edict forbade collection of public and private debts from one cash up to ten thousand in return—all collection was forbidden.
idiomatic: On gengxu day, the new moon of the eighth month, an edict forbade collection of public and private debts from one cash up to ten thousand in return—all collection was forbidden.

literal: day jiwei: Attendant-in-ordinary, Grand Tutor Li Yanshi, was made Minister over the Masses.
idiomatic: On jiwei day Li Yanshi, attendant-in-ordinary and grand tutor, was made minister over the masses.

literal: day dingmao: Regional Inspector of Guazhou Yuan Tairong was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongyang.
idiomatic: On dingmao day Yuan Tairong, regional inspector of Gua, was enfeoffed Prince of Dongyang.

literal: day jiaxu: Attendant-in-ordinary, Grand Guardian Yang Chun, resigned office.
idiomatic: On jiaxu day Yang Chun, attendant-in-ordinary and grand guardian, resigned office.

literal: day yihai: an edict ordered Grand Master of the Right Splendid Carriages Xi Yi to confer by plaque ranks on officers under Pillar of Heaven Grand General Erzhu Rong and Grand Preceptor Tianmu and on elders among fathers, uncles, and brothers, with differing governorships.
idiomatic: On yihai day an edict ordered Xi Yi, grand master of the right splendid carriages, to confer by plaque ranks on officers under Pillar of Heaven Grand General Erzhu Rong and Grand Preceptor Tianmu and on elders among fathers, uncles, and brothers, with differing governorships.

literal: Ninth month: Grand Commander Hou Yuan attacked Han Lou at Ji, defeated and beheaded him.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Grand Commander Hou Yuan attacked Han Lou at Ji, defeated and beheaded him.

literal: Youzhou was pacified.
idiomatic: You was pacified.

literal: Moqi Chounu attacked the city of Eastern Qin, took it, and killed Regional Inspector Gao Zilang.
idiomatic: Moqi Chounu attacked the city of Eastern Qin, took it, and killed Gao Zilang, regional inspector.

literal: Tenth month of winter, day dingchou: former Minister of Works, Prince of Danyang Xiao Zan, was made Minister over the Masses.
idiomatic: On dingchou day in the tenth month of winter Xiao Zan, former minister of works and Prince of Danyang, was made minister over the masses.

literal: Eleventh month, day jimao: Jiudexing of Yingzhou sent envoys asking to surrender.
idiomatic: On jimao day in the eleventh month Jiudexing of Ying sent envoys asking to surrender.

literal: day dinghai: an edict ordered all officials on leave or stationed outside to come to court, with differing deadlines.
idiomatic: On dinghai day an edict ordered all officials on leave or stationed outside to come to court, with differing deadlines.

literal: day bingwu: Grand Marshal, Minister of Works, Prince of Chengyang Hui, was made Grand Guardian; Minister over the Masses, Prince of Danyang Xiao Zan, was made Minister of Works; Commissioner with Credentials of the Third Rank, Regional Inspector of Yong Changsun Zhi, was made Minister over the Masses.
idiomatic: On bingwu day Hui, grand marshal, minister of works, and Prince of Chengyang, was made grand guardian; Xiao Zan, minister over the masses and Prince of Danyang, minister of works; Changsun Zhi, commissioner with credentials of the third rank and regional inspector of Yong, minister over the masses.

literal: Twelfth month, day xinhai: Zhang Jingyou, regional inspector of Yan under Xiao Yan; Li Lingqi, regional inspector of Jing; and Xiong Xin General Xiao Jinming came to surrender.
idiomatic: On xinhai day in the twelfth month Zhang Jingyou, Xiao Yan's regional inspector of Yan; Li Lingqi of Jing; and Xiong Xin General Xiao Jinming came to surrender.

literal: First month of spring of the third year, day jichou: Regional Inspector of Yi Changshou Shou and Regional Inspector of Liang Yuan Jun and others sent generals with Commander Yuan Jingxia, who campaigns at Ba, to attack Yan Shixin and behead him.
idiomatic: On jichou day in the first month of spring of the third year Changshou Shou, regional inspector of Yi, and Yuan Jun, regional inspector of Liang, and others sent generals with Yuan Jingxia, commander who campaigns at Ba, to attack Yan Shixin and behead him.

literal: Xiao Yan's commanders Xiao Wan, He Nanwei, and Chen Chou were defeated and fled; Wan's head was cut off and more than ten thousand were captured.
idiomatic: Xiao Yan's commanders Xiao Wan, He Nanwei, and Chen Chou were routed; Wan was beheaded and more than ten thousand taken.

literal: day xinchou: the people of Dongxu city, Lü Wenxin and Wang She and others, killed Regional Inspector Yuan Taibin and held the city in rebellion.
idiomatic: On xinchou day the people of Dongxu city, Lü Wenxin and Wang She and others, killed Yuan Taibin, regional inspector, and held the city in rebellion.

literal: General Who Guards the Army, Director of the Ministry of Punishments Fan Zihu, was made concurrently Right Vice Director and mobile-circuit attendant, supervising General Who Campaigns South, Commander Jia Xianzhi, and General Who Campaigns East, Regional Inspector of Xuzhou Yan Sida, to attack them.
idiomatic: Fan Zihu, general who guards the army and director of the ministry of punishments, was made concurrently right vice director and mobile-circuit attendant, supervising Jia Xianzhi, general who campaigns south and commander, and Yan Sida, general who campaigns east and regional inspector of Xu, to attack them.

literal: Second month, day jiayin: it was taken.
idiomatic: On jiayin day in the second month it was taken.

literal: Eastern Xu was pacified.
idiomatic: Eastern Xu was pacified.

literal: Third month: Chounu's grand mobile-circuit Yuchi Pusa raided Qi province; Grand Commander Heba Yue and Kezhun Hun Daoyuan greatly defeated him.
idiomatic: In the third month Yuchi Pusa, Chounu's grand mobile-circuit attendant, raided Qi; Grand Commander Heba Yue and Kezhun Hun Daoyuan greatly defeated him.

literal: Fourth month of summer, day dingsi: Minister of Works, Prince of Danyang Xiao Zan, was made bearer of the staff of authority, commander of the armies of Qi, Ji, and Yan provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, commissioner with credentials of the third rank, and regional inspector of Qi.
idiomatic: On dingsi day in the fourth month of summer Xiao Zan, minister of works and Prince of Danyang, was made bearer of the staff, commander of the armies of Qi, Ji, and Yan, grand general of agile cavalry with credentials of the third rank, and regional inspector of Qi.

literal: day dingmao: Regional Inspector of Yong Erzhu Tianguang attacked Chounu and Xiao Baoyin at Anding, defeated and captured them, and sent them imprisoned to the capital.
idiomatic: On dingmao day Erzhu Tianguang, regional inspector of Yong, attacked Chounu and Xiao Baoyin at Anding, defeated and captured them, and sent them imprisoned to the capital.

literal: day jiaxu: because Guanzhong was pacified, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On jiaxu day, because Guanzhong was pacified, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

literal: Chounu was beheaded in the marketplace; Baoyin was granted death at the Camel-Ox Office.
idiomatic: Chounu was executed in the marketplace; Baoyin was granted death at the Camel-Ox Office.

literal: Sixth month, day wuwu: an edict said that kin of the Hu clan who had received titles at court were demoted and attached to the registered populace.
idiomatic: On wuwu day in the sixth month an edict said that kin of the Hu clan who had received titles at court were demoted and attached to the registered populace.

literal: [9] The state of Yanda presented one lion.
idiomatic: [9] The state of Yanda presented one lion.

literal: That month Hu Wang Qingyun of the dried-up White Horse Dragon Pool usurped the great position at Shuiluo city, [10] and installed the hundred offices.
idiomatic: That month Qingyun, king of the Hu at the dried-up White Horse Dragon Pool, usurped the great position at Shuiluo city, [10] and installed the hundred offices.

literal: Seventh month of autumn, day bingzi: Tianguang pacified Shuiluo city, captured Qingyun, and buried alive seventeen thousand of its people.
idiomatic: On bingzi day in the seventh month of autumn Tianguang pacified Shuiluo city, captured Qingyun, and buried alive seventeen thousand of its people.

literal: day guisi: the people Ge Qiu and Bu Tangshi of Xiao Yan led fortified hamlets in submission.
idiomatic: On guisi day Ge Qiu and Bu Tangshi, people of Xiao Yan, led fortified hamlets in submission.

literal: day gengzi: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank Li Shuren, for an offense was stripped of name and made a commoner.
idiomatic: On gengzi day Li Shuren, grand general of chariots and cavalry and palace attendant of the third rank, for an offense was stripped of name and made a commoner.

literal: Ninth month, day xinmao: Pillar of Heaven Grand General Erzhu Rong and Prince of Shangdang Tianmu came to court from Jinyang.
idiomatic: On xinmao day in the ninth month Pillar of Heaven Grand General Erzhu Rong and Prince of Shangdang Tianmu came to court from Jinyang.

literal: day wuxu: the Emperor killed Rong and Tianmu in the Mingguang Hall, and Rong's son Bodhi, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
idiomatic: On wuxu day the emperor killed Rong and Tianmu in the Mingguang Hall, and Rong's son Bodhi, palace attendant of the third rank.

literal: Then the Chongxu Gate was raised; an edict said:
idiomatic: Then the Chongxu Gate was raised; an edict said:

literal: Heaven's Way abhors excess; human norms detest evil; what is loose is not left out, and punishment knows no sparing.
idiomatic: The Way of Heaven hates fullness; human custom hates wickedness—nothing loose escapes, and punishment does not spare.

literal: Thus at the gates of Lü and Huo calamity was the place of retribution;
idiomatic: So at the gates of Lü and Huo retribution found its seat;

literal: in the houses of Liang and Dong the omen of guilt stood forth.
idiomatic: in the houses of Liang and Dong the sign of guilt appeared.

literal: Lately at the end of Xiaochang the heavenly step was greatly perilous; the empress dowager disturbed government and the regent state had no lord.
idiomatic: Recently, as Xiaochang closed, the throne's step was dire; the empress dowager threw government into chaos and the regency had no ruler.

literal: Erzhu Rong came from Jinyang sharing worry for the royal house; when the banner of righteousness was raised, a great assembly met at Meng Ford; the age joyfully pushed him forward and together they completed the great enterprise.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong came from Jinyang with shared grief for the royal house; when the banner of righteousness rose, hosts gathered at Meng Ford; the age gladly pushed him on, and together they built the great work.

literal: Judging his first design, it was not without labor and effect.
idiomatic: In his first intent there was real toil and result.

literal: But to reach far yet fear being mired, to finish is in truth hard; before a morning was honored, the jackal's cry was already exposed.
idiomatic: Yet to aim far is to fear sinking in the end—and finishing is hard indeed; before the court could honor him a full morning, his jackal voice was already plain.

literal: At the Heyin campaign he could bear to be without kin.
idiomatic: At Heyin he could slaughter kin without flinching.

literal: Kings, dukes, ministers, and gentry perished in a morning; kin within and without were utterly destroyed.
idiomatic: Kings, dukes, ministers, and officers died in a single morning; kin inside and outside the house were wiped out.

literal: Borrowing heaven's authority, he nearly endangered the sacred vessel.
idiomatic: Wielding borrowed heavenly mandate, he nearly overturned the sacred vessel.

literal: Matters were hurried and there was no leisure to inquire into guilt.
idiomatic: Events rushed on; there was no moment to call him to account.

literal: Soon, because Ge's bandits ran rampant and horse heads turned south, faults were set aside and achievement demanded to pacify the ugly foe.
idiomatic: Soon Ge's rebels ran wild and armies turned south; faults were set aside and success demanded to crush the foul enemy.

literal: When Yuan Hao questioned the tripod and the great carriage toured north, again he roused troops loyal to the throne and showed strength where action was needed.
idiomatic: When Yuan Hao seized the tripod and the imperial carriage toured north, again he mustered loyal arms and pressed his strength where the need lay.

literal: Judging by this merit, it might yet have made up for faults.
idiomatic: Measured by that service alone, one might say his faults were partly redeemed.
